title: Pre-Construction Marine Finance
h1: NOT CONFIRMED - the search link title for the page is 'Pre-Construction Marine Finance' [a][b]; the H1 itself was not revealed
summary: Silver Oak Capital's page describes funding arranged before physical construction starts on a new-build vessel (usually a yacht or superyacht). The facility covers early costs - shipyard signing deposit, design and project-management fees, long-lead equipment ordered early, yard slot reservations - because a standard marine mortgage cannot be used while the asset does not legally exist yet. The firm says it specialises in this and provides the liquidity to fund shipyard stage payments; once the build starts the facility often rolls into stage-payment (construction) finance drawn in tranches. A separate /faq/ answer says pre-construction finance is typically interest only, with monthly interest serviced on funds drawn and capital repaid or refinanced into a mortgage on delivery. No loan sizes, rates, durations, timescales, lender counts, testimonials or CTAs for this page were revealed. Related marine pages add: export credit market for new builds, yachts typically over 20m, British/Cayman/BVI/Maltese registers, 1.00% broker fee and an old 'up to 70% LTV' indicative example (dated ~700 days old, possibly outdated).
